behaviors.behavior: a found promotion is delivered as its own small PR against the default branch, and the local (triggering) branch is reset back to its pre-promotion HEAD, untouched
a ledger-only promotion (no code change) is still committed and delivered as its own PR
an already-open promotion PR causes this sweep to skip the push and report not_delivered rather than opening a duplicate
a push failure still resets the local branch back to pre-promotion HEAD
a `gh pr create` failure (after a successful push) still resets the local branch
a push timeout degrades to not_delivered and still resets the local branch
an unreadable/empty pre-promotion HEAD sha is reported as rollback_failed rather than silently skipping the reset
the final rollback reset's own returncode is checked -- a failing reset is reported rollback_failed with a CRITICAL warning, never swallowed as success
an unreadable pre-sha (rev-parse HEAD failure) bails out before any `git add` is run, so nothing is ever staged against an unknown base
a commit failure after staging rolls back the staged residue (best-effort hard reset) instead of leaving the worktree dirty
the promotion sweep is invoked during worktree setup and its warnings (including a delivered promotion's PR url) surface in setup's own warnings[]
the promotion sweep runs BEFORE the canon self-heal + outbox sweep, so its own push never ships an unrelated self-heal/outbox commit riding along on the shared ancestry
